title: Head, IT Audit
description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Job Title: Director, IT Audit Department: Internal Audit Reports to: Chief Audit Officer About this role The Director, IT Audit provides strategic leadership for the organization’s technology audit function. This executive role oversees comprehensive risk assessments, evaluates IT governance and cybersecurity controls, ensures strict regulatory compliance, and advises executive leadership and the Audit Committee on mitigating technology risks across enterprise infrastructure, applications, and cloud environments. Responsibilities Audit Strategy & Planning: Develop and execute an annual, risk-based IT audit plan aligned with corporate business objectives, regulatory requirements, and emerging technology trends. Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Assessment: Direct complex audits covering network security, cloud architecture (Google/AWS), identity and access management (IAM), data privacy, and business continuity/disaster recovery. Governance & Compliance Frameworks: Evaluate alignment and compliance with industry frameworks including ISO 27001, NIST, COBIT, SOC 2, and applicable data privacy laws (e.g., GDPR, NDPR). Executive Leadership & Governance: Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of IT auditors and technical specialists. Foster continuous professional development and technical proficiency. Reporting & Stakeholder Management: Present audit findings, comprehensive risk evaluations, and practical remediation plans directly to the Chief Audit Officer and Senior Executive Management. Continuous Monitoring & Analytics: Drive innovation by embedding automated audit techniques, data analytics, and continuous controls monitoring (CCM) into the overall audit lifecycle to enhance efficiency. Experience & Background 10+ years of progressive experience in IT auditing, technology risk management, or cybersecurity, including 4+ years in a senior leadership/management role. Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, or a related quantitative discipline. Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA) required. Additional credentials such as CRISC, CISM, CISSP, or CIA are highly desirable. Deep technical understanding of cloud environments (Google & AWS), network infrastructure, database security, API, application controls, and IT General Controls (ITGCs). Skills & Competencies Exceptional stakeholder management, executive presence, oral and written communication, strategic problem-solving, and conflict resolution skills. Strong proficiency in risk assessment prowess and deep thinking. Advanced predictive & prescriptive data analytics skills. Self-driven capacity, agility, customer obsession, professional skepticism, and urgency. What success looks like in this role Establishment of a robust, proactive, risk-based IT audit strategy that protects enterprise assets and cloud infrastructure. High-performing, technically proficient IT audit team delivering clear, high-impact evaluations and actionable remediation plans. Continuous integration of automated audit controls, analytics, and full compliance with industry regulatory standards and frameworks. Why join us  Competitive compensation, benefits, and career growth opportunities.  Fully remote work culture and support for professional development

title: Head of Credit, Kenya
description: About us Ranked in 2024 by the Financial Times, Moniepoint is Africa's fastest growing fintech, trusted by over 10 million business and individual accounts, processing billions of naira in transactions monthly. Our mission is to enable financial happiness for every African, everywhere. About this role The Head of Credit, Kenya owns Moniepoint's credit business in Kenya: who we lend to, on what terms and at what price, and running the credit unit economics profitably within the risk appetite. They own the value proposition and unit economics of every credit product in Kenya, starting with SME lending to our merchant base and also consumer base. They work with the Head of Business in Kenya and functionally with the Group Head of Product, Credit. They write the briefs (RFC) for product architects and engineering to build the product and lending experience. Responsibilities Set the credit strategy for Kenya: which segments to serve, which credit products to offer, and how to price for risk, starting with SME lending to Moniepoint merchants and then consumers. Own the credit unit economics in Kenya, covering interest and fee, cost of funds, credit losses, and operating costs, with the budget, forecast, and reporting that give the Head of Business and Group Head of Credit clear visibility. Design credit value propositions with sound unit economics, grounded in evidence of what Kenyan businesses (and eventually for consumers) need and in what is already proven in Nigeria. Apply the Group credit policy framework in Kenya, and agree local risk limits and pricing changes with the Group Head of Credit and Risk & Compliance. Make sure every Kenya credit proposition is validated with in depth customer contacts before the RFC goes to product architects, and that every credit RFC meets the RFC standard. Work with Data Science to define what a good underwriting decision looks like in a thin-file market, and keep tightening it using portfolio performance. Work with Growth on distribution, deciding how credit reaches customers through direct sales, the merchant base, and partner channels. Make sure the credit business complies with Kenyan regulation from the start, including Central Bank of Kenya lending rules, credit reference bureau reporting, and data protection. Experience & Background Over 7 years of experience in fintech and ideally in lending specifically in Kenya. Direct ownership of a lending unit economics, with the ability to explain the full economics of a portfolio you ran and how you balanced growth against portfolio quality. Track record of building or scaling an SME (or comparable) lending book, ideally in a market with thin credit history data. Experience launching credit products in a new market or business, from first disbursement to scale. Experience leading lending teams across portfolio management, credit operations, and collections. Experience working with product, data science, and risk teams to turn credit needs into clear requirements and better underwriting. Skills & Competencies Deep understanding of how a lending business makes or loses money, and of SME credit needs. Strong grasp of credit risk and lending economics: pricing for risk, cost of funds, loss rates, vintage and roll-rate analysis, and collections. Able to interrogate a credit model's output rather than simply consume it. Disciplined at framing credit bets as hypotheses and validating them before scaling. Ability to shape the work of functions you do not own through influence and a clear commercial point of view. Strong analytical skills, comfortable using data and AI-assisted tools. What success looks like in this role A clear credit strategy for Kenya agreed with the Head of Business and Group Head of Credit. The credit book growing to plan in disbursement and revenue, with credit losses within the agreed risk appetite. Credit products meeting contribution margin targets. Every Kenya credit RFC meeting the RFC standard and moving to build with little rework. Clean regulatory standing with the Central Bank of Kenya, and accurate credit reference bureau reporting. Why join us Build a credit business from the ground up in one of Africa's most dynamic markets. Serve SMEs that remain underserved by credit despite Kenya's advanced financial infrastructure. Apply a model already proven at scale in Nigeria, with the backing of the Group credit team. Work in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment with significant responsibility.

title: Head of Debt Collections
description: About Moniepoint Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions and process over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. JOB PURPOSE The Head, Debt Collection is a strategic leadership position tasked with the architecture and execution of Moniepoint’s debt collection framework. The primary focus of this role is the minimization of Loss Given Default (LGD) within both the business and consumer lending divisions.   The incumbent will oversee, develop, and implement comprehensive and versatile debt collection strategies designed to manage a diverse portfolio of credit products, ranging from digital-first retail lending to large-ticket corporate financing.   Responsibilities include designing the organizational structure of the debt collection unit and recruiting high-caliber talent. Additionally, specialized expertise in debt litigation and asset recovery will be required to navigate complex cases of delinquency.   A data-driven methodology must be utilized to systematically evaluate the efficacy of recovery tactics and the performance of personnel.   Job Responsibilities  Design and implement a segmented debt collection framework — differentiated by product type, ticket size, and delinquency stage — spanning early-stage soft collections through hardcore legal recovery, restructuring, and write-off pathways. Define the org structure, recruit high-caliber talent, and stand up the operational and systems infrastructure (collections management systems, tracking dashboards, agent/dialer tooling) needed to run recovery at scale. Direct legal recovery strategy for the department — whether executed directly or through instruction of external counsel — ensuring all actions comply with applicable financial regulations and debt collection laws. Manage high-level engagements with external stakeholders, including law enforcement agencies, regulatory bodies, and external counsel, to expedite resolution of non-performing loans (NPLs). Design incentive structures and performance frameworks (KPIs, commission or fee structures) for the collections and recovery network to drive both recovery rate and cost-to-collect efficiency. Continuously train and upskill the collections and recovery network in alignment with collections  strategy and industry best practice. Own collections and recovery performance reporting to senior management, including recovery rate, cost of recovery, and portfolio-level LGD trends, and feed recommendations into credit committee decisions on write-offs and restructuring. Collaborate with credit, legal, risk, and finance to align collections and recovery efforts with underwriting standards and portfolio strategy. Qualifications Bachelor's degree in a relevant field. Minimum 7 years of experience in credit/debt recovery, including senior leadership of a recovery function handling high-value non-performing loans. Demonstrated experience across both high-ticket/corporate recovery (litigation-led, relationship-driven) and high-volume digital/retail collections (analytics-led, behavioral, tech-enabled)  Strong working knowledge of debt recovery laws, banking regulations, and court procedures in Nigeria. Familiarity with digital collections infrastructure and tactics — dialer/CRM systems, SMS/USSD/app-based nudges, propensity-to-pay scoring, and behavioral segmentation for low-ticket, high-volume portfolios. Demonstrated experience designing, building, or scaling a recovery/collections function — including org design, systems and process build-out, and team hiring. Proven experience overseeing recovery operations with national coverage, including a strong network of legal counsel and law enforcement contacts spanning all six geo-political zones in Nigeria — as opposed to experience confined to a single state or region. Excellent negotiation, problem-solving, and decision-making skills. Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret financial and portfolio data to guide recovery strategy. Relevant Skills Loan Recovery & Collections Strategy (high-ticket and digital/retail) Credit Risk Management Data Analytics, Propensity Scoring & Portfolio Reporting Digital Collections Tools & Automation Negotiation & Conflict Resolution People & Performance Management Organisational Design & Team Build-out What we can offer you Culture -We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. We’ve built a company where all opinions carry weight and where all voices are heard. We value and respect each other and always look out for one another. Above all, we are human. Learning - We have a learning and development-focused environment with an emphasis on knowledge sharing, training, and regular internal technical talks. Compensation - You’ll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, annual bonus, plus other benefits. What to expect in the hiring process A preliminary phone call with the recruiter An interview with one of our credit business leads A behavioral and technical interview with a member of the Executive team.  Moniepoint is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates.

title: Head of Operations & Compliance Audit
description: About us Ranked in 2024 by the Financial Times, Moniepoint is Africa's fastest growing fintech, trusted by over 24 million business and individual accounts, processing billions of naira in transactions monthly. Our mission is to enable financial happiness for every African, everywhere. About this role The Head, Operations & Compliance Audit is responsible for leading, managing, and executing comprehensive, risk-based internal audit engagements across operational, financial, compliance, and corporate support functions of Moniepoint Microfinance Bank. Grounded in professional standards (IIA, CBN Guidelines), you will provide independent, objective assurance and consulting services to Executive Management and the Board Finance, Audit & Risk Committee (FARCO). The primary mandate is to evaluate and enhance the effectiveness of governance, risk management, internal controls, financial reporting integrity, regulatory compliance, and operational efficiency across all assigned domains. Responsibilities Develop, execute, and continuously update the annual risk-based internal audit plan for all assigned business units and supporting functions, aligning with the Bank's risk assessment framework. Provide strategic insights to senior management and the Board Audit Committee on material risks, control weaknesses, and emerging exposures. Drive continuous auditing, data analytics, and automation to improve audit coverage, detect revenue leakage, and identify duplicate or unauthorized ledger postings. Lead and develop a high-performing team of auditors overseeing finance, fraud management, regulatory compliance, and branch operations. Evaluate the design and operating effectiveness of Internal Control over Financial Reporting (ICFR) across core banking and ERP modules, as well as bank-wide cost optimization frameworks. Oversee fraud risk screens, assess anti-fraud controls and whistle-blowing mechanisms, and ensure immediate escalation of established fraud cases. Evaluate compliance with Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) regulations, the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 (NDPA), and Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CFT) frameworks. Manage routine and unannounced audits across the branch network, vendor lifecycle, corporate governance processes, and enterprise marketing spend. Ensure all working papers, audit programs, compliance tests, and draft reports adhere strictly to IIA Standards. Experience & background Minimum of 12-15 years progressive internal audit, control, or risk management experience within Financial Services (Fintech, Microfinance Banking, Deposit Money Banks). Minimum of 5 years in a senior supervisory or managerial role leading internal audit teams. Proven track record in revenue assurance, financial controls, branch operations audit, and regulatory compliance. Minimum of a Bachelor's Degree (B.Sc. / HND) in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or related fields (Master's Degree is an added advantage). Skills & competencies Mandatory professional qualification such as ACA, ACCA, CPA, or equivalent; specialized certifications (CIA, CISA, CFE, or CRISC) are highly preferred. Deep understanding of CBN regulations, MFB Prudential Guidelines, Consumer Protection Framework, AML/CFT Regulations, NDPA, and IIA International Standards. Advanced expertise in exploratory, predictive, and prescriptive data analytics and automated audit working paper tools. Sound knowledge of core banking systems, general ledger integrity, financial statements, and payment workflows. Uncompromising integrity, unwavering commitment to independence, and exceptional executive communication skills for board-level (FARCO) reporting. What success looks like in the role A comprehensively executed annual risk-based internal audit plan that aligns perfectly with the Bank's risk framework. Quality assurance, working papers, and draft reports that adhere strictly to IIA Standards. Proactive assessment of risks and accurate immediate escalation of material exposures and fraud cases to the CAO and Management. High-performing and continuously developing internal audit teams delivering cross-functional process audits that successfully identify control gaps and bottlenecks. Why join us Shape the governance, risk management, and operational efficiency of one of Africa's fastest-growing fintechs. Provide strategic, board-level impact by directly advising the Board Finance, Audit & Risk Committee (FARCO) and Executive Management. Lead diverse audit portfolios ranging from financial and regulatory compliance to enterprise marketing and branch operations.

title: Head of Personal Banking Sales Network
description: Who we are Ranked in 2024 by the Financial Times, Moniepoint is Africa’s fastest growing fintech, trusted by over 10 million business and individual accounts, processing billions of Naira’s in transactions monthly. Our mission is to enable financial happiness for every African, everywhere. Moniepoint is Africa's all-in-one financial ecosystem, empowering businesses and their customers with seamless payment, banking, credit, and management tools. In 2023, we processed $182 billion and are Nigeria's largest merchant acquirer. About the Role The Head of Personal Banking Sales Network is an experienced sales professional who owns the retail sales distribution engine for personal banking. This is a network leadership role, not an individual selling role and you will be required to build, motivate and control a large independent contractor field force and the regional management layer above it. You will be measured on qualified customer acquisition and product penetration delivered at a defensible cost per unit.  Duties & Responsibilities Own end-to-end performance of the sales team: deliver the acquisition and transaction target through the field sales channel. Own agent productivity: acquisitions per active agent per month, share of field agents performing 100% vs target, and time to first sale for new agents. Own network health: active agent count, attrition, reactivation and coverage in priority cities Design and maintain territory structure, prioritising penetration in priority cities. Set recruitment targets for each city/cluster and ensure delivery versus the target. Own cost per acquisition through the sales channel, including commission, incentive and field support. Design commission and incentive structures that reward activated and transacting customers, not registrations. Ensure full compliance with all legal and regulatory requirements. Own the field sales performance routines: daily check-ins, weekly regional reviews, monthly business reviews. Requirements 10 - 15 years in field sales leadership, with at least 5 years leading regional sales leaders. Direct experience running a distributed agent, agency or independent contractor network of significant scale. Proven ownership of a commission or incentive scheme, including designing it and defending its cost. Strong command of sales analytics: funnel conversion, productivity distribution, cohort based performance. Strong people leadership skills: training, motivating and managing a large field sales team Experience operating in financial services, telecoms, FMCG distribution or another high volume regulated or semi regulated industry. Willingness to travel across regions regularly. Preferred Qualifications Experience in banking, payments or lending distribution in Nigeria. Experience in building and scaling a field sales team Familiarity with sales enablement tooling and CRM based territory management. About You You’re calm, objective, and grounded, even in high stakes situations. You balance empathy with fairness and have strong judgment on what’s “right” versus what’s “easy.” You communicate with clarity and confidence, building trust at every level. You think systemically and you see patterns behind cases and design solutions that prevent recurrence. You value compliance but see your role as enabling business success, not blocking it. What Success Looks Like Delivery against monthly and annual first transaction targets from the sales channel. An implemented plan to increase agent output, featuring defined benchmarks and measurable tactical growth drivers. Established field sales performance routines, including weekly and monthly reviews, executed against standardized templates with disciplined action tracking. Optimized cost per new active customer, trending within the approved thresholds.

title: Implementation Officer (Abia)
description: Who We Are Moniepoint is Africa’s all-in-one financial ecosystem, empowering businesses and their customers with seamless payment, banking, credit, and management tools. In 2023, we processed $182 billion and are Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer. We are on a mission to create financial happiness for everyone, everywhere. What We Do At Moniepoint, we are a customer-focused community dedicated to crafting solutions that redefine our industry. We leverage artificial intelligence and data-driven best practices to support our businesses, from providing credit and overdrafts to ensuring every transaction is secure. Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? Check out our stories on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth. Job Title: Implementation Officer Reports To: Lead, Onboarding Location: Abia - Aba North, Aba South, Umuahia North Work Mode: Hybrid Employment Type: Outsourcing Job Purpose The Implementation Officer ensures new retail customers successfully adopt Moniebook POS into their daily store operations through structured, high-touch onboarding experiences. This role bridges the gap between sales and long-term customer success by transforming newly signed customers into confident, active users who derive maximum value from the platform within their first 30-60 days. Operating as the customer's primary guide during the critical early adoption phase, you will understand each retailer's unique operational needs, configure Moniebook to fit their workflow, deliver effective training, and drive product adoption that sets the foundation for retention and expansion. Activation rates, time-to-value, feature adoption depth, and seamless handoffs to Account Managers measure success. Key Responsibilities Onboarding Program Design & Execution: Create and execute tailored onboarding plans that guide customers from signup to full operational usage. Define clear milestones, timelines, and success metrics for each customer's onboarding journey. Product Setup & Configuration: Guide customers through initial Moniebook POS setup. Training Delivery & Enablement: Conduct engaging live training sessions (both one-on-one and group) that educate retail staff on core Moniebook features, best practices, and operational workflows. title: Product Auditor
description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. What We Do At Moniepoint, we are a customer-focused community dedicated to crafting solutions that redefine our industry. We leverage artificial intelligence and data-driven best practices to support our businesses, from providing credit and overdrafts to ensuring every transaction is secure. Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? Check out our stories on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth. Role Overview The Product Auditor provides independent assurance over the design, implementation, and operating effectiveness of product controls across payment, wallet, settlement, switches and other related products across the organisation The role ensures that new and existing products are deployed with adequate financial, operational, security, and regulatory controls, safeguarding the organization against revenue leakage, settlement failures, regulatory breaches, and technology-driven risks. The Product Auditor will independently evaluate product risk exposure and control maturity prior to scale. Key Responsibilities  Audit Universe & Risk-Based Planning Maintain a living Product Audit Universe covering all payment products, features, and integrations ranked by risk.  Own the annual Product Audit Plan, ensuring coverage is allocated dynamically based on risk ratings, product complexity, regulatory sensitivity, and change velocity. Product Design & Control Assurance Review PRDs, business rules, and transaction workflows to identify logic gaps, unmitigated risk paths, and missing exception-handling routines before products reach production/go-live.  Analyse product path scenarios, verify Maker-Checker enforcement, and provide formal control design sign-off before any material release goes live. Live Product Assessment ( Continuous Audit Review) Periodically assess live payment products to confirm they continue to operate within approved design parameters.  Detect configuration drift, identify silent divergence from original PRDs, and analyse live transaction data for emerging risk patterns. Go-Live Readiness & Control Gate Execute mandatory pre-production Product Audit reviews as an independent control gate for all material releases.  Confirm reconciliation logic, exception queues, and fallback controls are tested and functional.  Escalate critical deficiencies with risk ratings and hold recommendations where a product is not safe to release. Transaction Logic & Mathematical Integrity Interrogate the Fee Engine using SQL to mathematically prove that commissions, VAT, discounts, and splits are posted with complete precision.  Validate duplicate prevention mechanisms and ensure transaction integrity within complex, multi-step payment sequences, and test reversal, refund, and chargeback logic to confirm financial symmetry is maintained in every scenario. Settlement & Ledger Integrity Trace fund flows, confirming continuous synchronisation between wallet sub-ledgers and the General Ledger.  Assess reconciliation logic for breaks and evaluate the authorisation, documentation, and reversibility of manual settlement overrides. Product Change & Configuration Integrity Confirm that all product modifications: fee tables, routing rules, limit parameters passed through an approved change management cycle.  Identify silent changes made outside formal release processes and audit the integrity of product master data to ensure it is access-controlled, version-tracked, and consistent with approved product terms. Vendor & Third-Party Product Risk Assess controls over vendor-managed product components, evaluate SLA performance against contractual commitments, and identify single-vendor dependency risks within critical payment flows.  Evaluate the organisation's ability to detect unilateral changes in third-party API behaviour, fee logic, or settlement processes. Control Advisory & Stakeholder Engagement Engage product and engineering teams early in the design cycle to provide informal control advisory, reducing findings at the formal review stage without compromising independence.  Participate in design reviews and architecture discussions, and build a control-by-design culture across product teams.  Incident Review, RCA & Regulatory Alignment Lead post-incident reviews for product failures,producing structured RCA reports that identify underlying logic failures, not just surface symptoms.  Assess corrective actions for adequacy and track findings to verify closure.  Ensure product logic complies with CBN guidelines, PCI DSS, and consumer protection obligations at the design level, and evaluate the regulatory impact of new features before release. title: Resident Internal Control Officer (RICO)
description: About Us: Ranked in 2024 by the Financial Times, Moniepoint is Africa’s fastest growing fintech, trusted by over 10 million business and individual accounts, processing billions of Naira’s in transactions monthly. Our mission is to enable financial happiness for every African, everywhere. About this role: The Resident Internal Control Officer is responsible for establishing a permanent, independent, on-site control presence at the assigned Moniepoint MfB branch. The primary objective is to monitor daily transaction integrity across all branch activities, mitigate operational risks, prevent and detect insider and outsider fraud, and ensure adherence to internal bank policies and procedures. Scope note: Loan origination, disbursement, recovery and portfolio review, cheque operations, and compliance activities (including KYC/AML reviews and regulatory reporting) are outside the scope of this role. All other products, services, and activities conducted at the branch fall within the RICO's remit. Where a RICO notices a suspected compliance or AML concern while carrying out control reviews, it is referred to the Compliance function without delay. Responsibilities 1. Daily On-Site Operational Controls Cash and vault controls: Perform daily vault, teller till, ATM/cash-recycler (where applicable), and petty cash counts, validating physical balances against the Core Banking Application (CBA) records and cash-in-transit documentation. Dual control and key custody: Enforce dual-control principles for vault access, cash movement, high-value transactions, and custody of keys, combinations, tokens, and sensitive stationery. Teller and counter operations: Review cash deposits, withdrawals, transfers, and teller end-of-day balancing for accuracy, correct authorisation, and adherence to transaction limits. Transaction and exception review: Review daily transaction logs, exception reports, reversals, backdated entries, and system overrides to detect unauthorised activity or breaches of approval limits. Reconciliation and general ledger: Verify timely reconciliation of settlement, nostro/correspondent, and inter-branch accounts; review suspense, sundry, and other control accounts for aged or unexplained items; confirm proper clearance. Deposit products: Test the accuracy of interest computation and booking on savings and fixed/term deposit accounts; verify early-liquidation approvals and rollover instructions. Account servicing: Review account maintenance activity, including mandate and signatory changes, BVN/NIN updates, account reactivation, dormant account handling, account closures, liens, and Post-No-Debit (PND) restrictions, to ensure each is properly authorised and supported. Electronic and agent channels: Monitor branch-linked electronic channels and services (POS, ATM, mobile/internet banking, USSD, agent banking) for irregular activity; control the issuance, activation, and custody of cards, PINs, and tokens. Staff and user access: Review system user profiles, access rights, segregation of duties, and staff account activity; flag dormant, shared, or excessive access. Assets and expenses: Verify physical asset registers and monitor branch operating expenses and procurement against approved budget limits. Physical security: Confirm that CCTV, alarms, strong-room integrity, cash-handling procedures, and the visitor register are functioning and in use. 2. Inspections, Investigations & Reporting Investigations: Conduct targeted investigations into cash shortages and overages, operational errors, customer complaints, and suspected staff collusion or fraud, preserving evidence and escalating in line with policy. Surprise checks: Carry out unannounced cash, vault, asset, and process checks, and risk-based sample testing across branch activities. Remediation tracking: Track and follow up on remediation plans issued by Head Office Internal Audit or external examiners, where they relate to branch controls, until closure. Examination support: Serve as the branch point of contact during internal audits and external examinations, coordinating document requests and responses. Incident escalation: Escalate material incidents, fraud events, and control breaches to the Regional Lead and the Head, Distribution Network Risk & Control immediately, in line with the incident escalation timelines. Findings and escalations are not subject to approval by branch management. Reporting: Compile and submit daily, weekly, and monthly control reports detailing branch risk trends, process gaps, control exceptions, and corrective actions taken. Experience & Background Education: Bachelor's degree or Higher National Diploma (HND) in Accounting, Banking & Finance, Economics, or a related business discipline. Experience: Minimum of 3 years' experience in internal control or internal audit within a Microfinance Bank, Commercial Bank, or Fintech company in Nigeria, with exposure to branch operations. Professional certification (any one of the following): CBN Microfinance Certification Programme (MCP) administered by the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria (CIBN). Associate of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria (ACA). Associate of the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria (ACIB). ACCA or CFE (Certified Fraud Examiner) will be an added advantage. Skills & Competencies Technical knowledge: Working knowledge of CBN guidelines for Microfinance Banks as they relate to branch operations and internal controls. Understanding of branch banking operations: cash management, deposit products, account maintenance, electronic channels, reconciliations, and general ledger controls. Hands-on experience with a modern Core Banking Application (e.g., Orbit, Finacle, T24, BankOne) and advanced Microsoft Excel; ability to analyse transaction data and exception reports. High moral integrity: Uncompromising ethical standards with zero tolerance for irregularities. Analytical mindset: Exceptional attention to detail and the ability to spot subtle patterns of fraud or process manipulation. Firm communication: Ability to stand one's ground objectively against peer pressure or branch management overrides, while communicating issues clearly to executive leadership. Independence and discretion: Maintains objectivity and confidentiality, and does not take part in the operational processes being controlled. Sound judgement and resilience: Works effectively under pressure and escalates promptly and appropriately. What Success Looks Like in This Role Zero unmitigated cash discrepancies, dual-control breaches, or unauthorized system overrides across daily branch operations. Early detection and swift escalation of potential insider or outsider fraud, protecting bank assets and customer trust. Timely, accurate submission of daily, weekly, and monthly control reports that provide clear visibility into branch risk trends. 100% closure of internal audit and external examination remediation items within agreed timelines. Strong, independent control governance maintained objectively alongside branch operations.

title: Rewards Specialist
description: Who we are Ranked in 2024 by the Financial Times, Moniepoint is Africa’s fastest growing fintech, trusted by over 10 million business and individual accounts, processing billions of Naira’s in transactions monthly. Our mission is to enable financial happiness for every African, everywhere. About the role Moniepoint is looking for an analytical Senior Associate, Compensation to join our global Rewards team. As we scale across multiple international entities, this new role will serve as the core analytical engine behind our cash compensation programs, salary structures, and cyclical pay operations.In this role, you will support the bi-annual pay reviews, performance bonus payouts, external market benchmarking, and job architecture maintenance. allocations Advanced Reward Modeling Perform analyses, including compa-ratio positioning, salary band spread design, and cost modeling, to evaluate the fiscal impact of compensation policies Market You'll partner with teams across the business to ensure our payment solutions meet real market demands and grow efficiently as we scale. Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? Check out posts on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth. title: Senior Principal, Talent Marketing
description: About us Ranked in 2024 by the Financial Times as Africa's fastest-growing fintech, Moniepoint is trusted by over 10 million business and individual accounts, processing billions of dollars in transactions monthly. Having built resilient, high-volume financial infrastructure that powers commerce across emerging markets, Moniepoint is embarking on its next phase of global scale. About this role As our Senior Principal, Talent Marketing, you will be the strategic architect responsible for establishing Moniepoint's talent brand and candidate pipeline in new markets from scratch. Where Moniepoint is not yet an established consumer brand, you will solve complex talent acquisition problems by understanding how senior engineers, engineering managers, and technical leaders think, connect, and evaluate career moves across Europe. Working from a blank piece of paper with high autonomy, you will translate our global Employer Value Proposition (EVP) into localized, high-converting talent marketing strategies. You will bridge the gap between Talent Acquisition, Engineering Leadership, and Brand - combining developer community immersion, high-touch physical events, and targeted campaigns that turn brand discovery into qualified, closed engineering hires.   Responsibilities 1. Zero-to-One Market Entry & Tech Hub Architecture Define European Hub Talent Strategy: Architect and lead the talent go-to-market strategy for Moniepoint's newest engineering hubs (principally Poland and Spain), crafting localized narratives that appeal to discerning software engineers. Anchor the 'Founding Team' Narrative: Position early European engineering cohorts as foundational builders, creating compelling narratives around technical scale, system complexity, and ownership that resonate with elite technical talent. Navigate Market Nuances: Diagnose and navigate country-specific developer dynamics—recognizing that developer communities in Poland, Spain, and the UK behave differently and require tailored engagement models rather than copy-pasted playbooks. 2. Developer Community, Ecosystem & Event Activation High-Impact Physical & Virtual Presence: Conceive, curate, and lead our physical presence at key developer conferences, engineering meetups, hackathons, and university partnerships across target markets. End-to-End Pipeline Activation: Ensure events are never vanity exercises; architect end-to-end follow-up systems and talent nurture funnels that convert event attendees into active, screened pipelines for our TA partners. Developer Platform Immersion: Leverage deep knowledge of where engineers consume information (e.g., GitLab/GitHub communities, tech forums, Discord/Slack groups, Meetup, Eventbrite) to drive authentic engagement. 3. Strategic Hiring Campaigns & Technical Enablement Targeted Campaign Architecture: Partner with TA leads and Engineering Directors to identify acute hiring bottlenecks and build agile, multi-channel marketing campaigns that address specialized, hard-to-fill tech disciplines. Technical EVP Translation: Translate technical architecture, distributed systems challenges, and fintech infrastructure realities into authentic, intellectually rigorous technical messaging that outshines local competitors. Recruiter Enablement & Narrative Toolkits: Equip our technical sourcing and recruitment teams with high-leverage narrative assets—outbound pitch decks, technical one-pagers, culture collateral, and messaging sequences that double recruiter outreach conversion. 4. Performance, Analytics & Optimization Hiring-Centric Metrics: Discard vanity metrics. Evaluate every initiative against pipeline contribution, qualified applicant rates, candidate quality score, cost-per-hire, and time-to-fill. Budget Oversight: Own and allocate dedicated talent marketing budgets with extreme commercial discipline—scaling programs that drive measurable hires and rapidly decommissioning initiatives that underdeliver. Paid Acquisition (Tactical Lever): Oversee and strategically deploy paid recruitment marketing spend across relevant technical platforms and channels when targeted outbound and community channels require acceleration. 5. Strategic Leadership & Scalability Strategic Thought Partnership: Serve as the trusted advisor to the Head of Talent Acquisition, VP of Engineering, and Brand Leadership on talent market intelligence, competitor positioning, and developer sentiment. Playbook Documentation: Establish and document Moniepoint's global talent expansion playbook, creating scalable frameworks that will be deployed across future international markets. Mentorship & Functional Growth: Provide strategic guidance to broader TA and brand team members, with the opportunity to mentor or direct junior talent marketing specialists as the function scales. Experience & Background 8+ Years of Talent Marketing Leadership: Experience leading talent marketing, technical recruitment marketing, or developer relations/advocacy, with substantial time dedicated to hiring software engineering and product disciplines. European Market Expertise: Demonstrated experience building talent brand presence and hiring pipelines across European tech ecosystems (particularly Central/Eastern Europe such as Poland, and Western/Southern Europe such as the UK or Spain). Zero-to-One Market Entry Track Record: Proven success entering new geographies or scaling talent brand where the employer brand was nascent or non-existent, creating playbooks from a blank sheet of paper. Fintech & Scale Exposure: Experience in hyper-growth fintech, high-frequency/payments infrastructure, or high-scale distributed systems environments. International Collaboration: Experience collaborating with international founding teams or distributed tech hubs across emerging and mature markets. Skills & Competencies Mastery in Event-Driven Pipeline Activation: Extensive hands-on experience designing and executing physical and digital developer events and architecting the subsequent candidate nurturing journey that yields hires. Deep Engineering Domain Fluency: Genuine understanding of software engineering culture, tech stacks (distributed systems, backend, infra, DevOps), and developer channels (Meetup, Eventbrite, GitLab/GitHub, Reddit, tech conferences). Comfort with Substantial Ambiguity: High agency and entrepreneurial drive; ability to make decisive bets, test hypotheses, and build structure in fast-moving, high-growth environments. Strategic Campaign Design: Ability to connect high-level EVP strategy to pragmatic, sprint-based talent acquisition sprints that deliver on an aggressive hiring plan (500+ tech hires). Paid Digital Campaign Optimization: Direct experience running and optimizing paid digital recruitment advertising campaigns independently across social and developer networks. What success looks like in this role First 30 Days (Discovery & Immersion): Map the competitive landscape and developer talent dynamics in Poland and Spain. Establish alignment with technical hiring leads (PEP, Engineering Directors) and TA leads to define immediate priority pipelines. Audit existing employer brand collateral and identify localized messaging gaps for European tech hiring. First 90 Days (Initial Market Entry & Quick Wins): Launch the first pilot physical event / developer meetup presence in Poland with a complete post-event pipeline conversion funnel. Roll out the European Recruiter Enablement Toolkit (localized pitch decks, outreach sequences, and technical one-pagers). Launch targeted marketing sprints for top 3 hardest-to-fill senior technical roles. First 6 Months (Hub Establishment & Pipeline Ramp): Position Moniepoint as a recognized, compelling engineering hub in Poland, supporting the identity and pride of the founding engineer cohort. Consistently contribute qualified, pre-warmed candidate pipelines directly supporting the ramp toward 500 tech/product hires. Prove multi-channel attribution showing which community and marketing initiatives are yielding quality hires. Year One (Global Expansion Playbook): Complete Moniepoint's International Talent Expansion Playbook, ready to be deployed across future tech hubs. Measurably decrease time-to-fill and increase direct outbound response rates across all European technical roles. Solidify Moniepoint's reputation as an employer of choice for Europe's most ambitious engineers. Why join us High-Impact Mission: Play a career-defining role in building the engineering backbone of Africa's fastest-growing fintech as it scales globally. True Ownership & Dedicated Resources: Autonomy to build from scratch with dedicated budget backing and direct executive sponsorship. Front-Row Seat to Tech Hub Creation: Help build engineering hubs from their inception, shaping culture, talent standards, and brand identity. Competitive Executive Package: Competitive base salary (calibrated for Senior Principal level), performance bonuses, comprehensive private healthcare, and pension schemes. Moniepoint is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates.

title: State Inventory Officer (Adamawa)
description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Job Title: State Inventory Officer Reports to: State Coordinator Employment Type: Outsourced Work Mode: Onsite About this role: The State Inventory Officer is responsible for managing the inventory of POS devices across the region, ensuring accurate tracking, secure storage, and efficient distribution. This role plays a critical part in operational success by validating serial numbers, monitoring stock levels, resolving inventory discrepancies, and collaborating with cross-functional teams to maintain seamless supply chain execution. Responsibilities: Inventory Management: Maintain accurate, up-to-date records of POS devices, including stock levels, locations, and serial numbers; monitor inventory to identify stock shortages and coordinate timely replenishment; conduct regular stock counts and audits to reconcile physical stock with logical inventory.  Serial Validation: Verify serial number accuracy for all received POS devices against corresponding records, promptly communicate discrepancies to relevant stakeholders, execute corrective actions, and maintain detailed documentation.  Discrepancy Management: Investigate and resolve discrepancies between physical and logical inventory, implementing corrective measures to prevent future errors and improve overall accuracy.  Collaboration & Communication: Partner with procurement, sales, and warehouse teams to optimize inventory operations and communicate inventory status, availability, and concerns effectively with internal stakeholders.  Additional Duties: Perform additional operational tasks as delegated and assigned by the State Coordinator.  Experience & Background: OND/HND or Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Business Administration, or a related field preferred.  Proven, similar experience in inventory management or related operational roles.  Skills & Competencies: Analytical & Problem-Solving: Strong capability to reconcile inventory discrepancies and identify process improvements.  Technical Proficiency: Skilled in using inventory management software and Microsoft Office applications.  Detail Orientation: Exceptional accuracy in data entry, record-keeping, and serial tracking.  Organization & Time Management: Ability to prioritize tasks, handle multiple operational demands, and meet deadlines.  Communication: Effective written and verbal communication skills across teams.  What Success Looks Like in This Role: 100% accuracy in POS device serial tracking and inventory records. Zero downtime in distribution caused by unmanaged stock shortages. Rapid, thorough resolution of physical vs. logical inventory discrepancies. Seamless alignment and clear communication with sales, procurement, and warehouse teams. Why Join Us? Competitive compensation, benefits, and career growth opportunities. Vibrant work culture and support for continuous professional development.

title: Team Lead, System Administrator
description: Who we are Moniepoint is an all-in-one financial services platform for emerging markets and the second-fastest-growing company in Africa. Since 2019, Moniepoint’s technology has powered over 3 million people, offering personal and business banking, payment, credit and business management tools to help them succeed. Moniepoint processed $182 billion in 2023, and currently processes the majority of the POS transactions in Nigeria.  Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? Check out posts on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth. About the Role The Team Lead, Systems Administration, is a senior individual contributor who also leads the IT infrastructure team tactically. This role is responsible for both the hands-on delivery of complex systems work and the orchestration of team priorities, standards, and output quality. The ideal candidate combines deep technical expertise in networking, cloud infrastructure, security, and automation with the leadership capability to coach a team, enforce SOPs, and drive measurable operational excellence, including leveraging AI tools to optimise how the team works. This role sits at the Team Lead level in Moniepoint's Talent Architecture. Success is defined not only by personal technical output, but by the team's consistent performance and delivery against infrastructure-wide targets. Scope & Decision Horizon Leads the IT infrastructure team tactically. Success is the orchestration of people and priorities to ensure the team's immediate output aligns with the broader roadmap. Principal Duties and Responsibilities Team Leadership & Operations Lead, coordinate, and coach a team of Systems Administrators, ensuring consistent output quality and adherence to SOPs. Manage team workload, prioritise tasks across competing demands, and ensure SLA compliance across all infrastructure functions. Conduct regular 1:1s, deliver direct and specific performance feedback, and actively develop team members' technical skills. Design and enforce team workflows and escalation paths, ensuring quality is consistent regardless of who executes the task. Own team-level metrics: system uptime (99.9%+), ticket SLAs, incident response times, and end-user satisfaction. Identify gaps in team capability or process and proactively close them through training, tooling, or workflow redesign. Infrastructure Management Design, implement, and maintain a robust IT infrastructure, including servers and virtualisation platforms (Proxmox). Administer and optimise Windows Server, Linux systems, and hybrid cloud infrastructures. Maintain comprehensive system documentation, network diagrams, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). Plan and execute system upgrades with minimal downtime; optimise for performance, reliability, and cost efficiency. Cloud & Network Infrastructure Design, deploy, and manage cloud network environments across GCP, OCI, and Azure, Outpost, including VPCs, subnets, peering, firewall rules, and private connectivity. Administer and optimise BGP routing policies, virtual routers (vRTF), and F5 load balancers across the enterprise network and cloud environments. Configure, manage, and troubleshoot enterprise networking infrastructure (routers, switches, firewalls, wireless access points). Implement and maintain network security protocols, VLANs, VPNs, and network segmentation across on-premise and cloud environments. Manage DNS, DHCP, Directory as a Service, and other core network services. Monitor network performance, analyse bandwidth utilisation, and implement QoS policies. AI Tools & Workflow Automation Manage, maintain, and evaluate AI tools used across the IT and infrastructure function, ensuring reliability, access control, and appropriate use. Build and maintain automation workflows using n8n and similar platforms to optimise repetitive operational processes. Design and implement AI-assisted workflows for network deployment, incident triage, and infrastructure monitoring. Coach team members on responsible AI integration, when to use AI tools, how to validate outputs, and where human review is required. Identify opportunities to reduce manual toil through intelligent automation and continuously improve the team's automation capabilities. Telephony & Unified Communications Administer and maintain the xCALLY PBX platform, including call routing, IVR configuration, queue management, and agent provisioning. Troubleshoot telephony incidents end-to-end: SIP trunks, PBX dial plans, voice quality, and carrier integration. Coordinate with ISPs and telecom carriers to ensure uptime and quality of voice services across all sites. Automation & Scripting Develop and maintain automation scripts (Python, PowerShell, Bash) to eliminate repetitive tasks and improve operational efficiency. Utilise Infrastructure as Code tools (Terraform, Ansible) for consistent and scalable infrastructure deployment. Build and maintain monitoring and alerting solutions using Prometheus, Grafana, and Nagios. Document automation and tooling clearly enough for an Associate-level team member to execute independently. Security & Compliance Implement and enforce IT security policies, access controls, and data protection measures across on-premise and cloud environments. Manage endpoint security solutions, patch management, and privileged access management. Manage user authentication systems, including SSO, MFA, and identity governance. Lead incident response: manage security events, conduct Root Cause Analyses (RCA), and implement permanent fixes. User Endpoint & Technical Support Oversee onboarding and offboarding procedures, ensuring seamless first-day experiences and complete account lifecycle management. Administer Google Workspace, including user provisioning, group management, Drive policies, and app integrations. Manage MDM solutions for corporate devices across Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android. Provide or oversee expert-level L2/L3 support, ensuring timely resolution and minimal user disruption. Manage IT asset inventory, lifecycle, and procurement coordination. Qualifications, Competencies & Skills Education & Experience Bachelor's degree or diploma in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field. 5+ years of proven experience in systems administration, infrastructure, or network engineering roles. At least 2 years of formal or informal team leadership, including coaching, delegation, and performance feedback. Relevant industry certifications (CompTIA, Cisco, Microsoft, GCP/Azure/OCI cloud, Linux) are highly desirable, but not compulsory. Technical Skills Advanced proficiency in Active Directory / Directory as a Service (e.g., JumpCloud); Linux/Unix administration (RHEL, CentOS, Ubuntu, Debian). title: Workforce Business Partner (Lagos)
description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. Job Title: Workforce Business Partner (Lagos) Reports to: Team Lead, Workforce Partner Job Purpose The Workforce Business Partner (WBP) serves as a strategic partner to business leaders, driving the alignment of people strategy with business priorities. This role exists to ensure that every people-related initiative — from performance enablement and workforce planning to leadership effectiveness — is executed with precision, empathy, and measurable impact. Beyond traditional HR delivery, the WBP acts as a trusted advisor, shaping organizational health and fostering a culture of accountability, engagement, and inclusion. The role bridges the gap between business needs and people solutions, ensuring that talent is positioned as a key enabler of growth and innovation. Key Responsibilities Partner with business leaders to translate organizational goals into actionable people plans that drive capability, performance, and retention. Lead workforce planning and organizational design discussions to ensure the right structure, roles, and talent are in place to meet current and future needs. Coach and influence leaders on talent strategy, performance management, and Independent Contractor engagement to strengthen leadership effectiveness and team culture. Act as a trusted advisor on IC relations matters, ensuring fair, consistent, and business-aligned resolutions in collaboration with the Workforce Relations COE. Analyze people data and insights to identify trends, risks, and opportunities, presenting data-driven recommendations to business leaders. Champion change management and communication strategies that support transformation, adoption, and continuous improvement within business units. Ensure compliance with internal policies and local labor laws while promoting a positive, high-performance culture.  Qualifications 2–4 years of progressive HR experience, including at least 2 years in a Business Partnership or advisory capacity. Demonstrated experience working in fast-paced, matrixed, or multinational environments. Strong understanding of core HR functions — performance management, people relations, organizational design, and workforce planning. Proven ability to use HR data and analytics to inform decision-making. Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting technical or commercial business units in a fintech, banking, or tech environment. Demonstrated success influencing senior stakeholders and leading complex change initiatives. About You You’re a strategic thinker who sees the big picture but executes with precision. You build trust quickly and communicate with empathy, clarity, and confidence. You thrive in ambiguity and can balance multiple stakeholders with ease. You’re data-driven — you make decisions grounded in insight, not intuition. You’re committed to continuous improvement, always seeking better ways to drive business impact through people. What Success Looks Like  You have established yourself as a trusted advisor to senior business leaders, influencing key people and organizational decisions. Business units under your support demonstrate improved engagement, retention, and performance outcomes. You’ve delivered a measurable improvement in workforce planning accuracy and performance management effectiveness. Leaders actively seek your input on strategic and people-related matters, not just HR processes. You’ve successfully embedded at least one COE-led initiative (e.g., new policy, performance framework, or workforce process) within your business unit with strong adoption and feedback. Why join us Competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and impactful career growth opportunities. Fully remote/flexible work culture backed by continuous support for your learning and professional development.

title: Workforce Relations Partner (North)
description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Job Title: Workforce Relations Partner (North) Reports to: Team Lead, Workforce Relations Job Purpose The Workforce Relations Partner is a strategic advisor and subject matter expert responsible for maintaining a fair, compliant, and high-performance workplace culture. This role exists to ensure that independent contractors relations practices not only mitigate risk but also strengthen trust, engagement, and organizational integrity across Moniepoint’s global operations. Will oversee the entire northern region. Beyond case management, the Workforce Relations Partner acts as a trusted advisor to business leaders and WBPs, providing thought leadership on policy interpretation, conflict resolution, and cultural alignment. The role balances business pragmatism with empathy and legal compliance, enabling leaders to make informed, people-centered decisions that reinforce Moniepoint’s values. Key Responsibilities Partner with leaders, Workforce Business Partners, Legal team and relevant stakeholders to resolve complex independent contractors relations cases with fairness, consistency, and business alignment. Provide expert guidance on disciplinary actions, grievances, investigations, and terminations, ensuring compliance with local labor laws and internal policies. Act as a strategic consultant to leadership teams, identifying systemic issues and recommending proactive interventions to minimize engagement risks. Analyze Workforce Relations trends, patterns, and case data to identify root causes, drive preventive strategies, and inform policy updates. Partner with the Employee Relations Partner to design, review, and implement employee relations frameworks, policies, and toolkits across entities. Build ER capability across the People Team and business leaders through coaching, education, and practical toolkits. Support change management initiatives and culture programs that foster open communication, inclusion, and psychological safety. Lead or support sensitive investigations involving complex or high-risk matters, ensuring due process and confidentiality throughout. Serve as a trusted voice of objectivity, balancing independent contractor advocacy and organizational needs in every decision. Qualifications 3–6 years of progressive HR or Employee Relations experience, including direct case management in a complex or regulated environment. Strong knowledge of labor laws and employment practices across multiple geographies (experience within Africa is an advantage). Proven experience managing investigations, conflict resolution, and policy enforcement. Excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to engage senior leaders confidently. Must reside in the North. Fluent in Hausa.  Preferred Qualifications Professional certification (e.g., CIPM, SHRM, or relevant Legal/ER specialization). Experience in fintech, banking, or other high-growth, multi-entity organizations. Demonstrated success implementing ER frameworks or leading cross-functional risk mitigation initiatives. About You You’re calm, objective, and grounded — even in high-stakes situations. You balance empathy with fairness and have strong judgment on what’s “right” versus what’s “easy.” You communicate with clarity and confidence, building trust at every level. You think systemically — you see patterns behind cases and design solutions that prevent recurrence. You value compliance but see your role as enabling business success, not blocking it. What Success Looks Like  You are recognized as a trusted advisor by business and HR leaders on complex ER and compliance matters. Consistent, fair, and timely resolution of Independent Contractors relations issues across all entities. Reduced recurrence of ER incidents through proactive coaching, early intervention, and data-led prevention. Enhanced ER literacy among managers and WBPs through structured education and guidance. Policies and practices are perceived as clear, fair, and aligned with Moniepoint’s culture and legal standards. Why join us Competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and impactful career growth opportunities. Fully remote/flexible work culture backed by continuous support for your learning and professional development.
